policy_title: Rebalance power dynamics in the food supply chain
stated: Rebalance the power dynamic between big food manufacturers and local alternatives, strengthen the powers of the Grocery Standards Adjudicator and Food Standards Agency, and regulate for fairness in negotiation and legally binding codes of practice.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for: • Rebalancing the power dynamic between big food manufactures and local alternatives such as local food networks, community-supported agriculture and other co-operatives. • Strengthening the powers of the Grocery Standards Adjudicator and the Food Standards Agency. • Reducing the vulnerability of the small-scale farming suppliers relative to the oligopolies in retail and food manufacture, by regulating for fairness in negotiation and new legally binding codes of practice.

bearing_set.reason: Food supply-chain regulation directly affects the costs and availability of food — an explicit O2 indicator — by shaping how pricing, terms, and margin are distributed between large manufacturers, local producers, and retailers, with a plausible (if contested) downstream effect on consumer food prices.

Legally binding codes of practice and stronger adjudicator powers reshape competitive dynamics in the food sector — protecting smaller/local producers' viability, supporting business dynamism and economic opportunity, while also potentially adding regulatory burden to larger operators; both sides move real indicators for prosperity and firm formation.

membership_note: The policy operates primarily as a B2B regulatory intervention in the food supply chain. O2 and O13 are the clear material bearings. O4 (worker conditions) is one step removed — the policy does not directly regulate employment terms. O14 (inequality) is plausible but the distributional mechanism runs through businesses rather than directly through household incomes and doesn't clearly meet the non-negligible bar without further specification.
